title: Rope Drop: Top parks open their Christmas holiday events
summary:
By Robert Niles: As the "rope drop" starts a day at theme parks, the Sunday "Rope Drop" post kicks off the week here at Theme Park Insider. Here is what lies ahead for fans at the parks this week.

This is the week that the nation's largest theme parks kick off their 2026 Christmas holiday events. Tonight also features the return of Mickey's Very Merry Christmas Party at Walt Disney World's Magic Kingdom. Here is the schedule, which you can find on our theme park events calendar page:

November 12 � January 3, 2027: Christmas Celebration at SeaWorld San Antonio
November 13 � January 3, 2027: Christmas Celebration at SeaWorld San Diego; Christmas Town at Busch Gardens Williamsburg
November 13 � January 4, 2027: Christmas Town at Busch Gardens Tampa Bay
November 13 � January 6, 2027: Holidays at Walt Disney World; Holidays at the Disneyland Resort
November 14 � January 3, 2027: Holidays at Universal Orlando Resort

Holiday events are underway already at SeaWorld Orlando, Dollywood and Silver Dollar City, which started their events this weekend.

We also have a few refurbishments happening this week:

November 9-10: Fyre Drill closes at Universal Epic Universe.
November 10: Space Mountain is closed at Disneyland.

In addition, Universal Orlando has added a refurb for Monsters Unchained at Epic Universe for December 11-15.

title: Walk Time: New coaster plans distract from tough financials
summary:
By Robert Niles: "Walk Time" is Theme Park Insider's Saturday look back at theme park news from the past week.

Six Flags and United Parks reported their third-quarter financial results this week. Both companies reported declining attendance and revenue, though the numbers were much worse at SeaWorld owner United than at Six Flags, which at least showed some promise on a same-park basis over the year to date.

United Parks also confirmed that SeaWorld Orlando's new dark ride, originally announced for this year, has pushed to 2027. The company also announced a memorandum of understanding for a potential new park in the Middle East. United already has licensed a SeaWorld on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, so this would be with a new partner. SeaWorld delays new ride as attendance drops across United Parks

The bigger news from Six Flags this week was its announcement that the upcoming season would be the last for California's Great America: Six Flags confirms 2027 closure for California's Great America.

Six Flags also confirmed this week that it is still looking at the possibility of selling more of its parks, as it looks to focus on its top performing properties. Six Flags reports flat attendance and smaller losses

One of those, the company hopes, will be Six Flags Magic Mountain in California. This week on the Theme Park Insider Podcast, Jake and I wishcast our ideas for what the park should include in the transformation plans that it has promised to announce next year. Podcast: Designing a better Magic Mountain

As for plans that are actually happening - or, at least, actually announced - The world's largest indoor wooden coaster is coming to Kentucky Kingdom and Universal announces new indoor coaster for Epic Universe.

Sticking with Universal, we got a look at what the park has planned for a new ride system in Universal files plans for its own hybrid boat coaster. Come for those plans, then stick around to make fun of the company's other patent application... for theme park NFTs.

Best wishes to everyone for a wonderful weekend! As always, thank you for being part of the Theme Park Insider community and for sharing links to our stories and content via email and social media.

title: Six Flags confirms 2027 closure for California's Great America
summary:
By Robert Niles: It's now official. The upcoming season will be the last for the California's Great America theme park.

Six Flags made the closure official today. The park's demise had been a fine deal for several years, after the former Cedar Fair sold the land underneath the park to developers in 2022. The park was allowed to continue operating under lease, however that lease expires in June 2028.

So Six Flags has decided that the 2027 season will be the final one for the Santa Clara theme park, which opened in 1976 as the west coast installation of Marriott's Great America. The park will close forever on Labor Day weekend in 2027.

"For more than five decades, this Santa Clara theme park has brought people together, created family traditions and served as the backdrop for unforgettable memories," Park Manager Dave Vosejpka said. "The Farewell Season is an opportunity for generations of Bay Area guests to return, spend time with family and friends, and revisit the attractions and traditions that have made the park in Santa Clara, California such a meaningful part of the community."

Six Flags will maintain its presence in the San Francisco Bay Area with Six Flags Discovery Kingdom, located across the bay in Vallejo.

title: Can a cartoon train a robot? Disney hopes so
summary:
By Robert Niles: Disney has a new plan to train robot performers at its theme parks. Just get the cartoons to do it.

Disney has deployed robots at its Disneyland theme parks in California, Hong Kong and Paris. Visitors to the Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge land have watched Disney's BDX droids shuffling around the land. In Hong Kong and Paris, a scale-appropriate Olaf character has wowed visitors to those park's World of Frozen lands.

Programming Olaf has been a challenge for Disney's Imagineers, which I wrote about after getting to spend some time with both Olaf and its creators at WDI headquarters in Glendale last year: Let's meet Disney's new Olaf and find out how he works.

One of the challenges for robots based on familiar, established characters such as Olaf is programming them to move just like their cartoon predecessors. Yet the laws of physics can be, uh, a bit more optional in the world of toons than they are in the real life of theme parks.

So Disney has detailed plans to use animation to help train a robot so that it can display the specific movements and gestures that the public has come to identify with that character. The trick is getting those to work with the physics of controlling a robot in an uncertain environment, where the machine must be able to react and maintain stability at all times.

You can read the details of Disney's proposal in its new patent application, Versatile Motion Priors for Artist-Directable Physical Characters. The proposal starts with traning a variational autoencoder on a kinematic motion dataset, such as from an animated film.

Again, you also can get an explanation of how Disney makes its Olaf walk-around animatronic, specifically, work in my earlier post, Let's meet Disney's new Olaf and find out how he works.

title: Universal adds new top annual pass level in Hollywood
summary:
By Robert Niles: Universal Studios Hollywood has added a new, fancier annual pass option.

The new Diamond Annual Pass costs $999.95 - a $400 increase over the previous top-tier Platinum Annual Pass. Like the Platinum, the new Diamond pass includes admission to the theme park every day of the year, plus free parking (except for after 6pm on Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays in April, May, September, and October). The pass also includes one free Halloween Horror Nights ticket, as well as discounts on CityWalk and on admission for friends and family.

So what does the $400 upcharge get you?

The Diamond Annual Pass includes one free admission to Universal Fan Fest Nights, which seems to confirm that the after-hours event will be back in 2027. The Diamond pass also gets you a 20% discount on in-park food, beverage and merchandise - up from the Platinum's 15%.

Beyond that, there are two big gets. First, the Diamond includes Universal Express access all day, as opposed to just after 3pm on the Platinum pass. The Diamond pass's fine print also does not explicitly exclude Fast & Furious Hollywood Drift like the Platinum pass fine print does. For either pass, this is the one-time per attraction per day Universal Express pass, not a Universal Express Unlimited pass.

Second, the Diamond pass includes one VIP Experience ticket, subject to blockout dates and availability.

Universal Studios Hollywood also offers Gold ($299.95), Silver ($219.95) and California Neighbor ($179.95) annual and season pass levels, with increasing numbers of blockout dates. Only the Gold pass includes free parking and in-park discounts. The California Neighbor is valid for nine months and is available to anyone, despite the implication of its name.

title: Universal files plans for its own hybrid boat coaster
summary:
By Robert Niles: Want to see Universal's plans for a hybrid boat ride system?

There's a new patent application from Universal, just published today. "Ride System With Vehicle for Suspension and Floating Operation" details Universal's plans for a hybrid boat and track ride.

In this ride system, boats would be suspended from an overhead track. When the ride vehicles reached the "boat ride" portion of the attraction, extenders coupled to the vehicle support would extend, allowing the vehicle to float in the water as they moved through the ride.

Even though the boats would be floating at this point, they would remain attached to the overhead bogie and the ride track.


Image from Universal's patent application

The effect of all this could be something similar ti the Mack Rides Rocking Boat system that made its U.S debut with Dollywood's NightFlight Expedition. That Mack Rides product had been tipped as the ride system for the new Epic Universe attraction that Universal Orlando announced this morning as a new indoor coaster. Could this system, described in Universal's new patent application, actually be the new Epic Universe Dark Universe ride system instead?

You can read the full description of what Universal has proposed in the patent application, Ride System With Vehicle for Suspension and Floating Operation.

Are we still doing NFTs?

Just for LOLs, here is another Universal patent application this week, Systems and Methods for Customized Non-Fungible Tokens Corresponding to an Amusement Park Attraction.

Yup, you could earn an NFT at a Universal theme park. NFTs caught well-deserved public derision for fueling a bubble within a certain segment of the recreational investment community a few years back. People lost a lot of money on the digital images, which are supposed to be uniquely identified and secured.

Universal's proposal seems like a way to create unique prizes for gameplay in the park, with Super Nintendo World immediately coming to mind, though interactive wands in The Wizarding World of Harry Potter could be used for this purpose, as well. Perhaps this is the appropriate use for NFTs, after all - as yet another worthless tchotchke in the universe of theme park prizes and souvenirs.

title: Universal announces new indoor coaster for Epic Universe
summary:
By Robert Niles: The expansion at Universal Orlando's Epic Universe is now official.

Universal Orlando Resort today announced that construction is underway for a new indoor thrill coaster in the Dark Universe land at Universal Epic Universe. The new coaster will "immerse guests in an all-new story inspired by the iconic Universal Monsters franchise" and be located next to the Monsters Unchained: The Frankenstein Experiment ride.

Beyond that, we did not get any additional details from Universal today. While construction is underway, Universal did not provide an opening date for the new coaster, other than to say that it will open "in the years ahead."

The new coaster will be the fifth at Universal's new theme park, which opened last year. Epic's Stardust Racers and Hiccup's Wing Gliders already claimed spots in Theme Park Insider readers' list of the world's top 40 coasters. The new coaster should continue to boost the appeal top coaster fans for the Universal Orlando Resort, which is home to our top-rated coaster, Jurassic World VelociCoaster at Islands of Adventure.

title: The world's largest indoor wooden coaster is coming to Kentucky Kingdom
summary:
By Robert Niles: Kentucky Kingdom will open the world's largest indoor wooden roller coaster next year, owner Herschend announced today.

Midnight Showdown will anchor the new Bluegrass Downs land at the Louisville theme park, which stands just a couple of miles away from Churchill Downs, the home of the world-famous Kentucky Derby. The Gravity Group will create the new horse race-themed coaster, which will feature 1,130 feet of wood track and stand more than three stories tall. The coaster will run two trains with 10 riders each.


Bluegrass Downs. Concept art courtesy Herschend

In addition to Bluegrass Downs, Kentucky Kingdom will retheme the area around this year's new Flying Fox coaster as Happy Valley Farm. That new land will include the Vekoma Suspended Family coaster as well as eight other "reimagined" rides, including Friendly Frogs, Loopy Lambs, and Country Cruiser.


Happy Valley Farm. Concept art courtesy Herschend

Herschend said that the new coaster and rethemed lands will complete the transformation of the park that the company began when it acquired Kentucky Kingdom in 2021. The company said that it has spent nearly $50 million to reshape the park in the past five years.
